entries.title: Mid-sized businesses can't leave quantum readiness to their suppliers
entries.summary: Mid-sized businesses cannot rely solely on major technology suppliers for quantum cyber readiness. Although suppliers set 2029 deadlines, they control only their own technology. Organisations should factor quantum threats into decisions on long-lived data and supplier choices now, as attackers already conduct 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks on sensitive information.

entries.title: New York’s AI Rules: Confidential Reports, Daily Fines, and a Kill Switch Wish List
entries.summary: New York's RAISE Act establishes regulatory framework for large AI developers. Companies with $500 million+ revenue must register with DIGIT by January 1, 2027, submit safety frameworks, publish them, pay fees, and report critical safety incidents within 72 hours. Non-compliance incurs $1,000 daily fines.

entries.title: The UK Considers Protecting Children From eBay by Checking Everyone’s Passport
entries.summary: UK government considers banning under-16s from second-hand selling platforms like eBay and Vinted to protect children from grooming and exploitation. Existing platforms already require age verification, though enforcement varies. Proposal originally announced in June, now expanded despite earlier assurances e-commerce sites were safe.

entries.title: The Microsoft outage is an urgent wake-up call for greater digital resilience
entries.summary: Microsoft November 13 outage highlighted fragility of internet infrastructure and risks from market concentration. Few corporations dominate digital services provision. Recent incidents include July 2024 Windows outage, October security vulnerabilities affecting 70% of websites, and September OpenAI AI agents hacking government infrastructure.

entries.title: FBI flash alert says Artex tool automating cyberattacks at ‘machine speed’
entries.summary: FBI alert warns that open source tool Artex automates cyberattacks at machine speed, reducing time from initial targeting to privileged access to under three hours.

entries.title: Chinese AI labs are training models on Nvidia's Blackwell despite export controls, says ex-OpenAI engineer
entries.summary: Forensic report identifies Nvidia's Blackwell processor fingerprint in AI models from Chinese labs including DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group, suggesting circumvention of export controls.

entries.title: Lawmakers Race to Renew Warrantless Spying Before January
entries.summary: US lawmakers attempt to renew Section 702 of FISA through the lame-duck session by attaching it to the NDAA, aiming to avoid a more privacy-friendly incoming Congress. Section 702 permits warrantless surveillance of foreigners abroad and incidental collection of Americans' communications, which agents can search without warrants. Civil rights groups oppose renewal.

entries.title: ASD SO/LIC Reorganized as Office of Strategic Services
entries.summary: The Assistant Secretary of Defense for Special Operations/Low-Intensity Conflict has renamed and reorganised his office as the Office of Strategic Services under an under-secretarial position. This represents a major Pentagon reorientation towards special operations and potentially exceeds Title 10 military authority.
